sheep.text: It chews, looks up, and regards you with deep sheep wisdom, which on closer inspection is a blank. A good blank. Very well maintained.

wall_mender.text: Mind your elbows, I'm mending the wall. A drystone wall is held up by weight and gravity and nothing else. Same as me.
The Mourne Wall took 18 summers and a small army of stone-men to build. They'd stop for the weather, I'm told, and then get on with the weather anyway.

shepherd.text: The sheep up here know where every gap in the wall is. We have a gentleman's agreement: they stay in, and I don't ask how.
A lamb's got more sense than a dog on a bad day. Don't tell the dog.

peat_cutter.text: Well now! Nobody comes in here without wading. Have a sit. The kettle's on, and so, I'm told, is the fog.
My granda cut peat on this very bog for the fire. These days we leave it wet to keep the carbon in. Same peat, newer manners.

mourne_rambler.text: I'm walking the whole of the Wall in a day. I'm on hour six. I'm on tile number... Look, there's a lot of wall.
The trick is snacks. Soda farl, a flask, and a heart full of denial.

then.text: A good job. Anyone who passes will think it was always there. That's the highest praise a wall gets.
There's the gap by the old stile. The sheep have been widening it for weeks. Fill it with what's lying about.
Read the plaque there when you're done. Then take word back to Nuala.

else.text: The Wall took from 1904 to 1922. The Belfast Water Commissioners wanted the sheep and cattle off the ground that drains into the Silent Valley, so the water would stay clean.
It crosses fifteen summits and it's about twenty-two miles long. No mortar. Big stones low, joints covered, a throughstone to tie it. Same as a team: no clever bits, only well fitted.
Men from round here built it, a summer at a time, with granite off the hillside. Nobody carved their name on it. You can find it in the way each length sits.
A wall's no good to anyone who hasn't heard about the people. Have a word with the weaver in Belfast first. She knows what hands are for.
